newsitem.title: NEPAL: China's Jiang ends South Asian visit.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang ends South Asian visit.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin left Nepal for home on Thursday at the end of a week-long visit to South Asia which he said aimed to foster peace and stability in the region.
Jiang was given a colourful farewell by Nepal's King Birendra, the world's only Hindu monarch, at the end of his two-day state visit to the Himalayan kingdom.
The Chinese leader's special Air China Boeing 747 aircraft took off to the Chinese national anthem and a 21-gun salute.

"China sincerely hopes to constantly enhance cooperation with South Asian countries for common development...and strive together into the coming 21st century for lasting peace and stability in this region and prosperity all over Asia," Jiang said at a state banquet in Kathmandu on Wednesday night.
Jiang began his rare South Asian tour in India last week before flying to Pakistan and later Nepal.

While Jiang was in New Delhi, China and India agreed to reduce troops on their disputed border, freeze cross-border military flights and avoid the use of force against each other. China and India fought a brief but bitter war in 1962.

In Pakistan, the Chinese president said instability in South Asia was a threat to the entire region. He pressed for a nuclear free zone in the region where India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947.
Both New Delhi and Islamabad are believed to be capable of making a nuclear bomb. China is a declared nuclear power.
Jiang, who arrived in Kathmandu on Wednesday, praised China's tiny Himalayan neighbour for "safeguarding national independence and state sovereignty."
During Jiang's visit, China pledged 560 million rupees ($10 million) in economic and technical aid to Nepal to mark King Birendra's 25 years on the throne.
Security was tightened for the visit in view of protests by Tibetan exiles in India.
Kathmandu recognises Chinese sovereignty over Tibet and bows to Beijing's sensitivities over Taiwan.
